info.text: Formative quiz for Chapter 3. From Think Python, 3rd edition, by Allen B. Downey (https://allendowney.github.io/ThinkPython/), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

questiontext.text: When you define a function, what are the variables that appear in parentheses?

feedback.text: An argument is a value you provide when you call a function.
A local variable is a variable that gets assigned a value inside a function.
A function object is the result of defining a new function.
A parameter is a variable that gets a value when the function is called.

questiontext.text: Which kind of statement can be used to run a line of code more than once?

feedback.text: An assignment statement assigns a value to a variable.
An import statement makes it possible to use functions in a module.
A print statement displays the value of an expression.
A for statement can run a line of code, or multiple lines, more than once.

questiontext.text:
What is wrong with this function, if anything?

def bottle_line(n, suffix):
    print(n)
    print('bottles of beer')
    print(suffix)

answer.text: Instead of def, the first word should be define.

feedback.text: def is the right keyword to define a new function, although some other languages use define.

answer.text: You can't have more than one parameter in parentheses.

feedback.text: You can have any number of parameters in parentheses, including none.

answer.text: Only the first statement of the body should be indented.

feedback.text: All of the statements in the body of the function should be indented.

answer.text: There are no errors in this function.

feedback.text: There is nothing wrong with this function.
